Brief 011 C · round 5 · production finish for v10

Sky: "really don't like our HUD. Should have the cell avatars, proper game professional sheen and framing." Same layout as v10 and Latch's build; what changes is the finish: framed enamel and chrome panels drawn with the image tool, the four real cell portraits (locked picks), crafted buttons with states. Step 1 of 2: pick a finish, then the sliceable kit.

5 · Flags, so Sky can choose knowingly

  • Height budget. The roster alone is 8.5% of screen height (92 px), at the edge of the 8%. With the verb plate above it the stack is 15% (about 160 px). Latch's placeholder is about 11%. The roster cannot shrink without the portraits dropping under 64 px (they are 66 px now). If the stack is too tall: put the verb plate left of the roster, or merge it into the roster's top rail.
  • Enforcer, reserved colours. The locked pick carries amber lenses and gold panels (1.7% of the portrait's pixels at 66 px sit within dE 12 of guard amber) and a violet collar lining (0.6%). It is small, but the amber lenses sit on a face where an enemy "guard" marker might be read. Suggested fix (shown in s3): smoke the lenses and pull the violet 65% to grey in the portrait only; the costume in the world stays as locked. The gold panels stay (locked).
  • Tech, selection. His cyan visor is the turquoise highlight (dE 2 to 5). Selection is therefore shape and value, not hue alone: a ring on the bezel with a white inner line, a tab above the window, and the other three portraits dimmed. See s1/s2, row "Selected: Tech". Open question for Sky: keep turquoise for selection (consistent everywhere else) or change to a warm white lamp.
  • Fixer likeness. The locked pick shows her mostly from behind and in profile, so her face here is generated from the hair, the dress and the turn of the head, not copied. She is recognisable by the long ponytail, the bare shoulders and the plum-and-cream top, not by a face the pick established. Her dress is dark plum, not violet; 0.0% of pixels read as rival violet.
  • Portraits are art direction, not final. Faces came from one generation per role from the references; Scout and Enforcer match the picks closely, Tech very closely (visor, locs, beard). Forma owns the character likeness; if she wants different faces the roster only needs new square images.
  • Panel colour. The generated chrome carried warm and purple reflections near amber and violet (up to 4.7% of the panel pixels). They are pulled to neutral in the composite; the kit export in Step 2 will bake the same fix. After the fix every panel pixel is at least dE 22 from the three signals.
  • No holograms, no touchscreen glass, no neon: the only lit things are the turquoise lamps, the cream alert lamps and the lit-text displays in the recessed windows (a soft bloom, as a lamp window). Lamps for Alert are cream, never amber.
  • What the mockups do not show: the investigator question mark and the dotted lead line (no investigator in these beats); pause and speed readouts; the hover dossier card.

6 · Glyph's top three

  1. r04 train-cab cluster. The round gauge windows crop the portraits tightly and hide the background field; the dark panel recedes so the street stays clear; knurled chrome knobs are the most crafted buttons here; and "instrument cluster" fits a clockwork city. Selected and hurt read clearly (s2). Weakness: the darkest, so it carries the least of the city's cream.
  2. r01 deco console. Cream enamel, seafoam end blocks and a chrome stringcourse are the city's own materials, so it sits in the street as if built there; square windows give the largest portraits. Weakness: cream on cream pavement is the lowest contrast, and the lamps are small.
  3. r02 chrome dashboard bar. The most "premium 1950s dashboard": a polished chrome bar with seafoam end caps and deep teal inset. Strong chrome sheen and good contrast on the street. Weakness: slightly bulkier ends; the round buttons are smaller than r04's.

Runner-up: r07 medallions (the friendliest, but each portrait loses the most area to its ring). Not recommended: r06 filmstrip (busy sprocket holes fight the portraits) and r09 sunburst (the rays crowd the verb plate).
